record.original_question: Does the fundamental biquandle classify virtual links up to mirror images, including the known ambiguity that the biquandle has the same value on the orientation-reversed mirror image obtained by reflection in a plane perpendicular to the diagram plane?

evidence.quote: Does the fundamental biquandle, see [124] classify virtual links up to mirror images?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a virtual link diagram is a 4-valent planar graph whose vertices are decorated as either classical crossings (with over/under information) or virtual crossings (drawn as a small circle), considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves (the three classical Reidemeister moves, the three purely virtual Reidemeister moves, and the mixed move). Virtual links are equivalence classes of such diagrams.

To an oriented virtual link diagram L one associates its fundamental biquandle BQ(L) as follows. The diagram is divided by the classical crossings into "semi-arcs" (an arc is broken at every classical undercrossing as well as at the two strands meeting at every classical crossing, but is not broken at virtual crossings). Assign one generator to each semi-arc. At each classical crossing one imposes two relations expressing the two outgoing labels as biquandle operations of the two incoming labels: if a, b are the under- and over-incoming labels and c, d the corresponding outgoing labels, then c = a^b and d = b_a (with the appropriate sign convention determined by the sign of the crossing). The resulting algebraic structure BQ(L), generated by the semi-arc labels modulo these relations, is an invariant of the oriented virtual link.

The "vertical mirror" of L is the virtual link L* obtained by reflecting the diagram in a plane perpendicular to the diagram plane (equivalently, by switching all classical crossings and reversing the orientation of every component). It is known that BQ(L) ≅ BQ(L*) as biquandles for every oriented virtual link L.

Question. Is the fundamental biquandle a complete invariant of virtual links up to this vertical-mirror ambiguity? That is, does BQ(L₁) ≅ BQ(L₂) (as biquandles) imply that L₂ is equivalent, as a virtual link, to either L₁ or its vertical mirror L₁*?
artifact.status_search_result: The completeness of the fundamental biquandle for virtual links (up to the known vertical-mirror ambiguity) is consistently listed as an open conjecture in the virtual knot theory literature. Recent surveys and problem lists on virtual knot theory still record it as unresolved, and current work focuses on biquandle-derived invariants (cocycles, brackets, quivers) rather than a proof of completeness.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Knot Theory – Unsolved Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the question of whether the fundamental biquandle classifies virtual links up to mirror images as an unsolved problem.
status_evidence.claim: Problem still appears on current unsolved-problem lists for virtual knot theory.

status_evidence.title: Bridging colorings of virtual links from virtual biquandles to biquandles
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work develops biquandle coloring invariants without resolving the completeness conjecture for the fundamental biquandle.
status_evidence.claim: Recent biquandle research does not claim a proof of completeness.
